key_insight: Floating-diffusion gain (~100 uV/e-) plus CDS reads ~1k-electron packets reliably. The transferable part is FD/CDS sensing for CCD strings and gain cells, not the pixel as a cell.
killer_doubt: The smallest shared CIS pixels are ~0.56 um pitch (~0.3 um2/bit) against DRAM's ~0.0017 um2: ~180x less dense. A 3 nm 6T SRAM bit (~0.021 um2) is 15x denser.
decisive_experiment: Free paper check: lay out a 2x2-shared 4T cell in a 65 nm CIS PDK and stop if it exceeds 0.05 um2/bit. Only then one CIS MPW (~$150k) measuring fill-and-spill write noise and 85 C dark charge.
prior_art: Near-duplicate of I-00973. Global-shutter CIS in-pixel pinned storage diodes (Sony, onsemi); Fossum pinned-photodiode/QIS jots; Phase B N-84 Jot-RAM (training knowledge).

key_insight: Pinning keeps the storage well away from every Si/SiO2 interface, cutting generation current ~1e4x below the 13 fA tail. What carries over is buried-channel storage for CCD strings.
killer_doubt: Retention is no longer the scarce axis: BEOL-stackable IGZO gain cells already reach aA-class leakage. A planar 3-4T pinned cell is ~0.3-0.5 um2, 200-300x DRAM's 0.0017 um2.
decisive_experiment: Planar needs no experiment, because the area math kills it. The only open path is N-84's 40 nm vertical well: a ~$30k TCAD check of 2-3e18 cm-3 pinning doping against BTBT onset at 0.5-1 MV/cm.
prior_art: Global-shutter pinned storage diodes (Sony, onsemi, ST); Teranishi/Fossum pinned photodiode; IGZO gain cells (imec, Kioxia) give aA leakage; Phase B N-84 Jot-RAM (training knowledge).

key_insight: Clean data with a valid backing copy can treat a decay error as a cache miss, as processors already do with parity-only clean L1 lines. Applied here to refresh policy.
killer_doubt: At 1-4 s, raw BER ~1e-5-1e-4 fails ~0.5-5% of 64-B lines. Flash refetch at ~80 us adds ~0.4-4 us average latency against ~100 ns DRAM.
decisive_experiment: On a DRAM Bender FPGA tester, hold refresh off for 1-4 s at 45-85 C and log line-failure rate and repeat-failure persistence (~$80k). If >0.1% of lines fail, refetch alone is dead and needs correction (I-07888).
prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011) critical/non-critical refresh split; parity-only clean cache lines refetched from L2 (IBM, Intel); RAIDR; Phase B N-64 lifetime-leased refresh (training knowledge).

key_insight: Per-cell Arrhenius slope plus bias dependence separates Poole-Frenkel, trap-assisted tunnelling and GIDL. Useful only as calibration data for refresh-relaxation models such as I-07888 and I-11108.
killer_doubt: No step change: refresh is 16-33% of idle power, so even halving the tail saves <=15%. Outsiders cannot act on it; vendors run deeper in-house EFA.
decisive_experiment: The study itself (~$300k): retention versus 45-95 C and wordline-off bias on ~1e5 weak cells from three vendors' DDR5 using DRAM Bender. Pass if signatures cluster into <=3 classes. Even a pass settles little.
prior_art: Hamamoto, IEEE TED 1998, retention distribution; Restle 1992 and Mori 2005 on VRT; Liu ISCA 2013 and REAPER 2017 on temperature (training knowledge).

key_insight: Refresh relief with zero hardware: storing the weak-page list in the SPD makes the profile travel with the DIMM. Deployable on any server that exposes a tREFI knob.
killer_doubt: VRT: Liu 2013 saw new failing cells appear for days, so one-shot profiling at 4x tREFI risks silent corruption. DDR5 on-die ECC hides weak cells. Saving ~3% server power.
decisive_experiment: Profile 20 DDR5 RDIMMs at 256 ms and retire failing pages, then run 30 days at 4x tREFI with ECC logging. Count new CE/UE per TB-day. Under $60k.
prior_art: RAPID (HPCA 2006) retention-aware OS placement; RAIDR 2012; REAPER 2017; BadRAM; HARP (on-die ECC profiling); Qimonda per-page refresh patent US7975170 (via search snippet).

key_insight: Lifetime-typed data could live in ms-retention cells with no refresh circuitry. The real lever, roll-to-roll layers at ~$1-5/m2, belongs to the long-retention R2R IGZO dossier I-01819.
killer_doubt: Ms windows hold little: KV pages live seconds to hours, training activations ~0.1-1 s, so likely <10% of capacity qualifies. Leaky-by-design oxide TFTs save nothing.
decisive_experiment: Histogram HBM capacity by data lifetime in PyTorch training and vLLM serving traces (<$50k). Proceed only if >30% of capacity lives under 10 ms; otherwise fold into I-01819.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs; PragmatIC IGZO FlexICs; RANA (ISCA 2018) refresh skipping for short-lived DNN data; this study's I-01819 (training knowledge).

key_insight: Anything pseudo-random need not be stored or refreshed. Dropout masks and random projection bases are already regenerated from RNG state today.
killer_doubt: Trained weights and KV are not seed-generated. Pseudo-random tensors are likely <1% of accelerator memory, and N-76 shows rate-distortion caps seed-coded weights at ~1.07-1.22x.
decisive_experiment: An audit is enough: count the bytes of seed-regenerable tensors in Llama-class training and serving memory snapshots (<$20k). Expect <1%.
prior_art: FlashAttention regenerates dropout masks from saved RNG state; PRANC, NOLA, VeRA seed-generated bases; RoPE computed on the fly; Phase B N-76 (training knowledge).

key_insight: Code against the 1% retention quantile, not the 1e-9 tail. Retention errors are one-way (Z-channel, ~4% parity bound); page-granular AI traffic tolerates codeword reads; line CRC gives a fast path.
killer_doubt: Decode cost: soft LDPC at ~1e-2 BER is est. ~1-5 pJ/bit and microseconds, against ~0.7 pJ/bit/s of refresh saved; it wins only for pages read less than every ~3 s.
decisive_experiment: DRAM Bender plus FPGA soft-LDPC (~$150k): age DDR5 rows 0.5-2 s at 85 C across data patterns and fit per-page error tails against Poisson. Pass if 15% parity gives page failure <1e-15.
prior_art: Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010); SECRET leaky-cell ECC (-87% refresh power); Qimonda per-page refresh US7975170. LDPC for DRAM refresh: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Temperature as the select signal: a 1.5 eV conductor gives ~1e14 on/off between 25 and 400 C, which would be a two-terminal access device with hours of retention.
killer_doubt: Prefactor bound: with sigma0 <=~1e4 S/cm, a 1.5 eV conductor at 400 C reaches ~6e-8 S/cm; charging 5 fF in 1 ns through 20 nm needs ~2.5 S/cm, ~4e7x more.
decisive_experiment: Free paper check: fit published sigma(T) for every candidate ionic or hopping conductor. Stop unless one reaches >1 S/cm at 400 C and stays <1e-12 S/cm at 85 C. Only then build a ~$100k microheater test chip.
prior_art: Thermally assisted MRAM (Crocus); ns PCM microheaters (IBM, Intel/Micron 3D XPoint). Arrhenius-gated DRAM access: none found (training knowledge).

key_insight: Hammer charge loss and leakage loss add in the same storage node, so one per-row deadline is the physically correct trigger. A leaky analog replica would track temperature for free.
killer_doubt: Without per-row retention profiles the time term is identical for every row: normal refresh plus PRAC. Profiles hit VRT, and refresh is only 16-33% of idle power.
decisive_experiment: Ramulator study driven by DRAM Bender per-row retention and hammer-coupling maps from 10 DDR5 chips (~$100k). Pass if debt-triggered refresh cuts refresh operations >=4x at equal UE rate, including VRT.
prior_art: JEDEC DDR5 PRAC per-row counters; RAIDR retention bins; Micron analog accumulator patents; Self-Managing DRAM (2022); this study's I-05623 analog integrator (R22).

key_insight: Clocked word planes shift packets through a semiconductor channel. Writes avoid the tunnel-oxide endurance wall, with no per-bit transistor, capacitor or staircase and one regenerator per hole.
killer_doubt: 60 bits x 3 phases = 180 transfers: at CTE 0.999, 16% of charge is lost. Far bit ~1-5 us away (NAND-class); poly-Si dark current forces constant clocking.
decisive_experiment: Merge into I-10793's test: a 16-32-tier IGZO vertical CCD in a university fab (~$400k) measuring per-transfer CTE, 85 C dark charge and gate cycling to 1e12. Drop the poly-Si variant.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory (IEDM 2024 planar, IMW 2026 vertical; per R16/R06 search logs); 1970s Intel/Fairchild CCD memories; Phase B N-08; I-10793.

key_insight: The target is right: select tiers with a shared broadcast signal instead of contacts, deleting the staircase and per-tier masks. Wavelength is the wrong carrier.
killer_doubt: Quantum dots absorb every photon above their gap, so the bluest pulse switches all 16 tiers. Light pipes need >=~300 nm pitch against DRAM's ~35 nm, ~70x area loss.
decisive_experiment: Paper first: show any narrowband selection scheme (e.g., plasmonic absorbers) in which the shortest-wavelength tier does not also fire, at <100 nm pitch. Otherwise a ~$50k two-tier PbS-dot stack confirms crosstalk.
prior_art: Multi-wavelength optical storage (spectral hole burning, holographic); QD photodetectors; staircase-free phase tying (I-02002). Optically addressed 3D DRAM tiers: none found (training knowledge).
